# Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs for Multi-turn Text-to-SQL with Multiple Question Types

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#mmsql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.17867v4) · arXiv:2412.17867v4, 8 April 2025

**Reading coverage:** All 10 actual PDF pages, sections I–VII, appendices A–C, tables I–VIII; rendered question-distribution and performance figures inspected. PDF text contained spurious form-feed glyphs, repaired by per-page extraction.

## Research question

Conversation turns require different behavior for answerable, ambiguous, unsupported and improper requests.

## Method

MMSQL combines refined CoSQL records with Gemini-generated QDA-SQL dialogues. A schema selector, question detector, decomposer and SQL refiner choose responses and generate/repair candidate queries.

## Evaluation

Eight base LLMs and three multi-agent variants are evaluated on a curated 149-dialogue test. SQL metrics and type classification are separate; TDEX scores SQL execution for answerable/ambiguous turns but type matching for other turns. GPT-4o-mini judges response quality, with a 100-sample human comparison.

## What the results support

The multi-agent configuration improves the reported aggregate scores, particularly for weaker baselines. Ambiguity classification and SQL after ambiguous requests remain challenging. Removing the detector hurts several measures; removing the refiner does not reduce every metric.

## Limits and qualifications

This evaluates curated/generated conversation records rather than uncontrolled real-user interaction. Class frequencies differ sharply between training and test. Prose reverses some Table V unanswerable/ambiguous precision-recall values, and Figure 3 execution numbers coincide with Table III exact-match values; avoid unqualified numeric comparisons.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A mixed-question routing benchmark; its hybrid TDEX and model-judged response quality need explicit interpretation.
